docs.title: AlphaFloor EFB User Guide
docs.text:
Welcome to the AlphaFloor EFB user guide. AlphaFloor EFB is an Electronic Flight Bag designed for Airbus aircraft in X-Plane 12. It provides complete operational flight planning, performance calculations, aircraft weight and balance management, charts, checklists, and ground servicing tools.

AlphaFloor EFB can be operated directly inside the 3D cockpit tablet or streamed over your local Wi-Fi network to any tablet, iPad, phone, or secondary monitor.

docs.title: Supported Fleet
docs.text:
AlphaFloor EFB is optimized for the following aircraft in X-Plane 12:

  • ToLiss A319 (CFM56 and IAE V2500)
  • ToLiss A320 (CFM56 and IAE V2500)
  • ToLiss A320neo (PW1100G and CFM LEAP-1A)
  • ToLiss A321 (CFM56 and IAE V2500)
  • ToLiss A321neo & A321XLR (PW1100G and CFM LEAP-1A)
  • ToLiss A330-900 (Rolls-Royce Trent 7000)
  • ToLiss A340-600 (Rolls-Royce Trent 500)

All aircraft configurations, fuel capacities, certified structural limits, and dataref interfaces are automatically detected when you load the aircraft.

docs.title: Operating Modes
docs.text:
1. 3D Virtual Cockpit Tablet: Operates directly on the pilot tablet screens mounted on the Captain and First Officer window frames. All buttons, tabs, and input fields respond to standard mouse clicks and scroll wheel movements.
  2. External Device (Wi-Fi LAN): Connect your iPad, Android tablet, phone, or secondary computer to the same local network as your simulation PC. Open the local address displayed in the EFB Settings to control the tablet with full touch gestures.

docs.title: Quick Navigation
docs.text:
• Installation Guide: How to install and verify the plugin.
  • Licensing & Free Trial: Starting your 7-day free trial, purchasing a lifetime license, and multi-device activation.
  • Interface & Controls: Cockpit interaction, status bar telemetry, and remote web access.
  • Applications Guide: Step-by-step instructions for each built-in EFB application.
  • Troubleshooting: Solutions for common setup and network issues.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This guide walks you through installing AlphaFloor EFB into X-Plane 12, verifying the setup, and configuring external tablet connections over your local network.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Flight Simulator: X-Plane 12 (version 12.00 or later).
  • Operating System:
  • Windows: Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit).
  • macOS: macOS Monterey (12.0) or newer (Universal binary natively supporting Apple Silicon and Intel).
  • Linux: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Debian 12, Fedora 38 or equivalent 64-bit distribution with standard glibc.
  • Supported Aircraft: Any of the supported ToLiss Airbus models installed in your X-Plane 12/Aircraft/ directory.

docs.title: 1. Download the Release Archive
docs.text: Download the latest universal release archive (AlphaFloorEFB-vX.Y.Z.zip) from the CyberPatate Website.

docs.title: 2. Extract and Move to the Plugins Folder
docs.text:
Extract the downloaded .zip file. You will see a folder named AlphaFloorEFB.

Move the entire AlphaFloorEFB folder into your X-Plane 12 plugins directory:

X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/

docs.title: 3. Verify Folder Structure
docs.text:
Confirm that the folder hierarchy looks as follows:

X-Plane 12/
\-- Resources/
    \-- plugins/
        \-- AlphaFloorEFB/
            |-- mac_x64/
            |   \-- AlphaFloorEFB.xpl
            |-- win_x64/
            |   \-- AlphaFloorEFB.xpl
            |-- lin_x64/
            |   \-- AlphaFloorEFB.xpl
            |-- config.json
            |-- user_checklists.json.example
            |-- skunkcrafts_updater.cfg
            \-- user-guide.pdf

Important: Do not rename the AlphaFloorEFB folder. Keep all files in their respective subdirectories.

docs.title: First Launch & Verification
docs.text:
1. Launch X-Plane 12.
  2. From the flight setup menu, load any supported aircraft (e.g., ToLiss A320neo or A321).
  3. Once the 3D cockpit finishes loading, look at the tablet mounted beside the Captain's window.
  4. The tablet screen will power on and display the AlphaFloor EFB home screen.
  5. Click anywhere on the screen with your mouse to interact with the applications.

docs.title: Connecting External Devices (iPad, Android, Laptops)
docs.text:
You can use any external tablet, iPad, smartphone, or laptop as a standalone touch EFB while flying.

  1. Connect your external device to the same local Wi-Fi network as your flight simulator PC.
  2. In the 3D cockpit EFB, tap the Settings icon on the bottom navigation bar.
  3. Locate the Remote Access (LAN) section. You will see an address such as: 
    http://192.168.1.42:8080
  4. Open your preferred web browser (e.g., Safari on iPad or Chrome on Android/PC) and enter that URL.
  5. The EFB interface will load with full touch functionality. Any action performed on the external device is instantly synchronized with the aircraft and the cockpit screen.

Tip for iPad users: In Safari, tap the Share button and select Add to Home Screen. This launches the EFB in full-screen mode without browser address bars.

docs.title: Updating AlphaFloor EFB
docs.text:
• Via SkunkCrafts Updater: AlphaFloor EFB includes full SkunkCrafts Updater integration. When an update is published, open the SkunkCrafts Updater window inside X-Plane to download and apply the update. Your license file and custom checklists are automatically preserved.
  • Manual Update: Download the new .zip package from the website and overwrite the contents of X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/. Your license file (AlphaFloorEFB.lic or license.json) will remain intact.

docs.title: Interface & Controls
docs.text: The AlphaFloor EFB interface is designed to emulate modern airline flight deck tablets while maintaining clean readability and minimal cockpit clutter.

docs.title: Cockpit Tablet Overview
docs.text: The EFB is mounted in the 3D cockpit on the Captain and First Officer side window frames. Both tablets can operate independently, allowing the crew to reference different screens simultaneously (e.g., Captain viewing Navigraph approach charts while First Officer computes landing performance).

docs.title: 1. Top Status Bar
docs.text:
The status bar remains visible across all screens to provide essential telemetry at a glance:

  • Clock Display: Displays current simulation time in both Local and UTC (Zulu) format.
  • Aircraft Telemetry: Shows active aircraft variant (e.g., A319, A320neo, A321LR, A330-900, A340-600) and airframe registration.
  • Network Status: Displays the local IP address and listening port for remote device connections.
  • Power & Indicators: Visual indicators for battery charge level and data synchronization status.

docs.title: 2. Main Content Area
docs.text: This central viewport displays whichever application is currently open (e.g., Performance Calculator, SimBrief OFP, Charts, or Checklists).

docs.title: 3. Bottom Navigation Bar
docs.text:
• Home Button (Left): Instantly returns to the application launcher grid from any screen.
  • Settings Button (Right): Opens the system configuration panel to adjust brightness, display themes, Wi-Fi options, or license settings.

docs.title: In-Cockpit 3D Interaction
docs.text:
• Left Click: Tap any button, tab, input field, or checklist item.
  • Mouse Scroll Wheel: Scroll through long flight plans, operational documents, or checklist pages.
  • Text Input: Click inside an input field (such as an airport ICAO code or gross weight) and type directly on your physical keyboard.

docs.title: External Tablet & Mobile Interaction
docs.text:
When viewing the EFB on an iPad, Android tablet, phone, or laptop:

  • Tap: Equivalent to a mouse click.
  • Touch Drag: Smooth inertial scrolling through checklists, flight logs, and weather reports.
  • Pinch to Zoom: Zoom in and out of georeferenced airport diagrams and enroute charts.
  • Orientation Support: The interface automatically reorganizes its layout when switching between landscape and portrait orientations.

docs.title: Licensing & Free Trial
docs.text: AlphaFloor EFB offers a transparent, pilot-friendly licensing model. You can test every feature without restriction for seven days before deciding to purchase.

docs.title: 7-Day Free Trial
docs.text:
Every pilot is entitled to a 7-day free trial with full access to all applications and calculations.

  1. Launch X-Plane 12 with any supported Airbus aircraft.
  2. If this is your first time loading the plugin, the license prompt appears on the tablet.
  3. Click Start 7-Day Free Trial.
  4. Your trial period begins immediately. An indicator at the top of the Settings screen displays your remaining trial days.
  5. You do not need to provide a credit card, email address, or account registration to use the trial.

docs.title: Purchasing a License
docs.text:
When you are ready to purchase a permanent license:

  • Price: 11.99 € (single one-time payment, lifetime license).
  • Store URL: https://cyberpatate.fr/alphafloorefb/
  • Payment Processing: Processed securely through Stripe using standard credit cards, Apple Pay, or Google Pay.
  • Updates Included: All minor and feature updates throughout the 1.x release cycle are included free of charge.

docs.title: Activating Your License
docs.text: After completing your purchase on the website, you will be redirected to an order confirmation screen. You have two convenient activation methods:

docs.title: Method 1: In-App License Key Entry
docs.text:
1. Copy the license key displayed on your confirmation screen (e.g., AFEFB-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX).
  2. In X-Plane 12, open the EFB tablet and tap the Settings icon.
  3. Select the License section.
  4. Paste or enter your key into the License Key field and click Activate.
  5. The status indicator will turn green and display Licensed (Full Version).

docs.title: Method 2: Standalone License File (AlphaFloorEFB.lic)
docs.text:
1. On your order confirmation screen, click the Download AlphaFloorEFB.lic button.
  2. Save the file directly into your plugin directory: 
    X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/AlphaFloorEFB.lic
  3. When you load the aircraft, AlphaFloor EFB automatically detects the file and activates your license without requiring manual key entry.

docs.title: Multi-Device Policy
docs.text:
• Up to 3 Personal Computers: Your purchase allows concurrent activation on up to three (3) personal computers (e.g., main flight sim desktop, laptop, secondary simulator rig) owned and operated by the same pilot.
  • External Tablets Do Not Consume Activations: iPads, Android tablets, phones, and laptops connected via local Wi-Fi to display the web interface are clients of your main simulator and do not count toward machine activations.

docs.title: Offline License Verification
docs.text: Once your license is verified, AlphaFloor EFB operates completely offline on your local computer. You do not need an active internet connection to fly or access any local performance and aircraft control features.

docs.title: Refund Guarantee
docs.text: If you encounter technical defects or hardware incompatibilities that cannot be resolved within 14 calendar days of your purchase, contact support at contact@cyberpatate.fr for a prompt, full refund.

docs.title: Troubleshooting & FAQ
docs.text: This section provides solutions for common setup questions, network connectivity, and troubleshooting tips.

docs.title: The tablet screen is black and does not turn on
docs.text:
• Verify Aircraft Electrical Power: The EFB requires aircraft electrical power. Ensure BAT 1 and BAT 2 are switched ON on the overhead panel, or that an External Ground Power Unit (EXT PWR) or APU is connected and supplying electricity.
  • Wake from Standby: If the tablet was previously switched off, click anywhere on the screen glass with your mouse to wake the display.

docs.title: My iPad or tablet cannot open the EFB web page
docs.text:
• Same Wi-Fi Network: Ensure your mobile device and simulation computer are connected to the exact same Wi-Fi router or subnet. If your phone or tablet is connected to cellular 4G/5G or a guest Wi-Fi network with client isolation enabled, it cannot reach the PC.
  • Firewall Permissions:
  • Windows: Open Windows Defender Firewall, locate X-Plane.exe, and ensure both Private and Public network access checkboxes are ticked.
  • macOS: Go to System Settings -> Network -> Firewall -> Options, and ensure incoming connections are allowed for X-Plane.
  • Verify IP Address: Simulation PCs can change IP addresses if your router reboots. Check the Settings screen on the cockpit tablet to confirm the current IP address.

docs.title: My SimBrief flight plan does not load
docs.text:
• Confirm that your SimBrief Username or Pilot ID is entered correctly in the EFB Settings without extra spaces.
  • Ensure you have actively generated an Operational Flight Plan (OFP) on SimBrief.com before clicking Fetch.
  • Verify that your simulation computer has an active internet connection.

docs.title: Navigraph charts do not display
docs.text:
• Verify that your Navigraph account has an active Charts subscription.
  • Go to Settings -> Navigraph, tap Sign Out, and complete the authentication process again using the QR code or device code.

docs.title: My license key shows "Invalid Key"
docs.text:
• Ensure there are no accidental spaces before or after the key when copy-pasting.
  • License keys follow the format: AFEFB-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX.
  • If you purchased recently, ensure your payment was completed successfully on Stripe.

docs.title: Standalone file AlphaFloorEFB.lic is not detected
docs.text:
• Verify that the file is placed directly in the main plugin folder: 
    X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/AlphaFloorEFB.lic
  • Make sure your operating system has not appended an extra extension (such as AlphaFloorEFB.lic.txt).

docs.title: Contact Support
docs.text:
If you encounter an issue not covered in this guide, our support team is available to assist:

  • Support Email: contact@cyberpatate.fr
  • Website: https://cyberpatate.fr/alphafloorefb/

docs.title: Aircraft Controls & Ground Services
docs.text: The Aircraft Controls & Ground Services application allows pilots to manage aircraft doors, ground servicing equipment, external electrical power, and refueling directly from the cockpit tablet.

docs.title: Doors & Hatches Management
docs.text: The application displays an interactive overhead schematic of the aircraft with real-time open/closed status for every door:

docs.title: Passenger Doors
docs.text:
• Door 1L: Main passenger boarding door (connected to jetway or boarding stairs).
  • Door 1R: Forward galley and catering service door.
  • Door 2L / 2R & 3L / 3R: Overwing emergency exits and mid-cabin doors (A321/A330/A340).
  • Door 4L / 4R: Aft passenger and service doors.

docs.title: Cargo Doors
docs.text:
• Forward Cargo Door: Opens the forward lower hold for luggage containers and pallets.
  • Aft Cargo Door: Opens the aft lower hold.
  • Bulk Cargo Door: Opens the rear bulk compartment.

docs.title: Quick Actions
docs.text:
• All Doors Open: Opens all doors simultaneously for rapid turnaround.
  • All Doors Closed: Closes and arms all doors prior to pushback.

docs.title: Ground Equipment Control
docs.text:
Toggle ground servicing objects when the aircraft is parked at the gate with engines shut down:

  • Wheel Chocks: Place or remove main gear chocks. (Ensure parking brake is set before removing chocks).
  • Safety Cones: Deploys standard turbine and wingtip ramp safety cones.
  • Ground Power Unit (GPU): Connects a ground power cart to supply 115V AC 400Hz electricity to the aircraft electrical network, allowing you to turn off the APU at the gate to save fuel.
  • Air Start Unit (ASU): Connects high-pressure pneumatic air for cross-bleed or external engine start if the APU bleed is inoperative.
  • Air Conditioning Unit (ACU): Provides pre-conditioned ground air to maintain comfortable cabin temperatures at the gate.
  • Passenger Stairs: Summons front and rear boarding stairs for non-jetway stands.
  • Catering Trucks: Drives catering scissor-lift trucks to galley service doors.

docs.title: Refueling Operations
docs.text:
• Request Fuel Truck: Calls the airport fuel tanker to the aircraft starboard wing.
  • Fueling Rate: Toggle between Instant Fueling (for quick flight setup) and Realistic Fueling (meters fuel at actual hydran pump delivery rates).

docs.title: Charts & Navigation
docs.text: The Charts application displays aerodrome diagrams, departure routes (SID), terminal arrivals (STAR), and approach plates directly on the tablet screen with real-time aircraft position overlay.

docs.title: Navigraph Account Linking
docs.text:
AlphaFloor EFB integrates directly with Navigraph Charts:

  1. Open the Charts application on the EFB.
  2. If not previously signed in, tap Sign in with Navigraph.
  3. A short device authentication code is displayed (e.g., ABCD-1234) alongside a QR code.
  4. Scan the QR code with your phone or visit https://navigraph.com/code on any device and enter the code.
  5. Confirm access on your Navigraph account.
  6. The tablet will automatically refresh and connect to the worldwide Jeppesen chart database.

docs.title: 1. Pinned Airports
docs.text:
When a SimBrief flight plan is active, AlphaFloor EFB automatically pins your:

  • Departure Airport
  • Destination Airport
  • Enroute Alternate(s)

Tap any pinned airport badge at the top of the screen to view its chart directory.

docs.title: 2. Manual Airport Search
docs.text:
To search for any global airport:

  1. Tap the search bar in the top navigation header.
  2. Type the 4-letter ICAO code (e.g., EGLL, EDDF, KSFO).
  3. Press Enter to view all available charts.

docs.title: 3. Chart Categories
docs.text:
Charts are organized into standard operational tabs:

  • TAXI: Airport diagrams, parking stand charts, low-visibility taxi routes, and hot spot advisories.
  • SID: Standard Instrument Departures.
  • STAR: Standard Terminal Arrival Routes.
  • APP: Instrument Approach Procedures (ILS, RNP, RNAV, VOR, Visual).
  • REF: Noise abatement, special departure procedures, and airport general notes.

docs.title: Interactive Chart Viewer Features
docs.text:
• Moving Map Position Overlay: On georeferenced taxi diagrams and approach plates, a magenta aircraft symbol indicates your exact real-time position and heading.
  • Day & Night Themes: Toggle between high-contrast daylight mode and dim night mode to preserve night cockpit vision.
  • Zoom & Pan Controls: Use your mouse scroll wheel and click-drag in the cockpit, or natural pinch-to-zoom gestures on external tablets.
  • Rotation: Rotate landscape and portrait charts with the 90-degree rotate button.

docs.title: Checklists
docs.text: The Checklists application provides interactive normal, supplementary, and emergency checklists designed to streamline cockpit workflows and improve situational awareness.

docs.title: Standard Checklist Flow
docs.text:
AlphaFloor EFB includes the standard Airbus flight phase operational checklist flow:

  1. Cockpit Preparation
  2. Before Pushback & Start
  3. After Start
  4. Taxi
  5. Before Takeoff
  6. After Takeoff (Climb)
  7. Cruise
  8. Descent Preparation
  9. Approach
  10. Landing
  11. After Landing
  12. Parking
  13. Securing the Aircraft

docs.title: Operating Checklists
docs.text:
• Checking Items: Click or tap any checklist line item. The item highlights in green with a checkmark, and the active cursor moves automatically to the next challenge-response pair.
  • Progress Tracking: A progress bar at the top of the checklist indicates completion percentage for the current phase.
  • Phase Navigation: Use the left sidebar to jump between flight phases as your flight progresses.
  • Reset: Click Reset Phase to clear items in the active checklist, or Reset All to reset all phases for a new flight leg.

docs.title: Custom Checklists (user_checklists.json)
docs.text:
You can fully customize the checklists to match your airline's specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) or virtual airline requirements:

  1. Locate the example template in your plugin directory: 
    X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/user_checklists.json.example
  2. Make a copy of this file and rename it to: 
    user_checklists.json
  3. Open user_checklists.json in any text editor. It follows a clean, simple JSON format:
{
  "phases": [
    {
      "name": "Before Pushback",
      "items": [
        { "challenge": "Cockpit Prep", "response": "COMPLETED" },
        { "challenge": "Gear Pins & Covers", "response": "REMOVED" },
        { "challenge": "Signs", "response": "ON / AUTO" },
        { "challenge": "ADIRS", "response": "NAV" },
        { "challenge": "Fuel Quantity", "response": "____ KG BALANCED" },
        { "challenge": "TO Data", "response": "SET" },
        { "challenge": "Baro Ref", "response": "____ SET CROSSCHECKED" },
        { "challenge": "Windows & Doors", "response": "CLOSED" },
        { "challenge": "Beacon", "response": "ON" },
        { "challenge": "Thr Levers", "response": "IDLE" },
        { "challenge": "Parking Brake", "response": "AS RQRD" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
  1. Save your changes. AlphaFloor EFB will automatically load your custom checklist on next launch, preserving it across software updates.

docs.title: Documents Viewer
docs.text: The Documents application allows flight crews to view PDF flight documentation, Quick Reference Handbooks (QRH), airline Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and Flight Crew Operating Manuals (FCOM) directly on the tablet screen.

docs.title: Adding Your Own Documents
docs.text:
To make custom PDF documents available in the EFB:

  1. Navigate to your AlphaFloor EFB plugin folder: 
    X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/documents/
    (If the documents/ folder does not exist, create it).
  2. Copy any standard .pdf files into this directory (e.g., A320_QRH.pdf, Company_SOP.pdf, Route_Briefing.pdf).
  3. Open or refresh the Documents application on the EFB. Your files will appear in the document library.

docs.title: Document Viewer Controls
docs.text:
• Document Library: Lists all available PDF files with file size and modification dates.
  • Page Navigation:
  • Tap the Next Page and Previous Page arrows to flip pages.
  • Use the Page Jump box to type a specific page number and press Enter.
  • Use the mouse scroll wheel for continuous vertical page scrolling.
  • Bookmarks & Table of Contents: For PDF documents with embedded outlines, tap the Bookmarks icon to jump directly to operational chapters (e.g., Engine Failure, Dual Hydraulic Loss, Cold Weather Operations).
  • Zoom & Pan: Adjust reading scale using the Zoom In/Out controls or pinch-to-zoom on an external tablet.

docs.title: Landing Performance Calculator
docs.text: The Landing Performance application calculates in-flight landing distances, approach speeds, and stopping margins for normal arrivals, crosswind operations, and diversions.

docs.title: Operating Overview
docs.text:
Prior to descent (during the arrival briefing):

  1. Select your destination or diversion airport and landing runway.
  2. Enter current runway surface conditions and reported winds.
  3. Choose your desired flap configuration and braking method.
  4. Tap Calculate Landing Distance.
  5. Review the resulting approach speeds, stopping distance, and runway remaining.

docs.title: 1. Runway Selection & Surface Condition
docs.text:
• Airport & Runway: Enter the destination ICAO and select the active runway to load the Landing Distance Available (LDA).
  • Surface Condition: Select according to the active METAR or ATIS:
  • Dry: Clean asphalt or concrete.
  • Good: Wet runway with damp or grooved surface.
  • Medium to Poor: Water pools, slush, compacted snow, or ice.

docs.title: 2. Aircraft Weight & Configuration
docs.text:
• Estimated Landing Weight (ELW): Read automatically from the aircraft datarefs or calculated from current gross weight minus planned trip fuel burn.
  • Flap Selection:
  • CONF FULL: Standard approach configuration for minimum landing distance.
  • CONF 3: Recommended for turbulent approaches or gusty crosswind conditions.
  • Thrust Reversers:
  • All Reversers Operative: Normal symmetric reverse thrust deployed at touchdown.
  • Idle Reverse Only: Noise-abatement operations or fuel conservation.
  • One Reverser Inoperative: Single-engine or MEL dispatch conditions.

docs.title: 3. Braking System Selection
docs.text:
• Autobrake LOW: Standard for long runways and gentle passenger deceleration.
  • Autobrake MED: Standard for medium or wet runways to ensure consistent deceleration.
  • Autobrake MAX: Short-field operations.
  • Manual Braking: Pilot-applied toe brakes with anti-skid protection.

docs.title: Calculation Results
docs.text:
After calculation, the application outputs:

  • Approach Speeds:
  • VREF: Landing reference speed based on landing weight and flap selection.
  • VAPP: Final approach speed, automatically factoring wind correction (minimum $+5\text{ knots}$, up to $+15\text{ knots}$ for headwind gusts).
  • Operational Landing Distance (OLD): Actual ground roll required from 50 ft crossing height to full stop.
  • Factored Landing Distance: Distance including standard regulatory safety margins (1.15x for in-flight assessment).
  • Runway Margin Remaining: Green badge indicating the remaining length of runway beyond the stopping point.
  • Overrun Warning: If the required stopping distance exceeds the available runway under selected conditions, an amber or red alert is triggered, advising an immediate change in flap configuration or diversion to a longer runway.

docs.title: Settings & System Configuration
docs.text: The Settings application configures display preferences, unit systems, remote network streaming, external account connections, and license activation.

docs.title: 1. Display & Cockpit Lighting
docs.text:
• Brightness: Adjust screen luminescence using the slider. In the 3D cockpit, this synchronizes with the tablet's physical brightness knob.
  • Theme: Choose between Dark Aero (optimized for night and dark cockpit environments) and Day Flight (high-contrast mode for bright daylight flying).
  • Display Units:
  • Weight: Toggle between Kilograms (KG) and Pounds (LBS).
  • Altimeter: Toggle between Hectopascals (hPa) and Inches of Mercury (inHg).

docs.title: 2. Remote Access (Wi-Fi LAN Streaming)
docs.text:
• Server Status: Indicates whether the local network server is active.
  • Local LAN Address: Displays the exact URL to type into your external tablet or phone browser (e.g., http://192.168.1.42:8080).
  • Connection QR Code: Scan the QR code with your mobile camera to open the EFB interface without typing IP addresses.
  • Port Configuration: Change the default listening port (8080) if you have other software utilizing that port.

docs.title: 3. Account Integrations
docs.text:
• SimBrief: Enter and save your SimBrief Pilot ID or username to automatically load dispatch flight plans.
  • Navigraph: View your Navigraph Charts connection status, authenticate new devices, or sign out.

docs.title: 4. License Management
docs.text:
• License Status: Displays your current entitlement:
  • Licensed (Full Lifetime Version)
  • Active Free Trial (X days remaining)
  • Trial Expired
  • Activate License: Input your purchased license key (AFEFB-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX) and click Activate.
  • License File Detection: Displays a checkmark if a standalone AlphaFloorEFB.lic file is active in your plugin folder.

docs.title: 5. Tablet Power Control
docs.text: • Switch Off EFB: Turns off the tablet display, returning the cockpit panel to its standby state. Tapping the screen or turning on cockpit battery power instantly restores the EFB.

docs.title: SimBrief Operational Flight Plan (OFP)
docs.text: The SimBrief OFP application integrates with your SimBrief account to display your full operational flight plan, fuel calculations, route waypoints, and weather reports directly in the cockpit.

docs.title: Setting Up Your SimBrief Account
docs.text:
1. Open the SimBrief app from the EFB home screen (or navigate to Settings).
  2. Enter your SimBrief Username or numeric Pilot ID.
  3. Tap Save & Fetch.
  4. AlphaFloor EFB will query the SimBrief API and load your latest dispatch package. Your username is saved locally, so you only need to enter it once.

docs.title: 1. Flight Overview
docs.text:
Displays critical flight details at the top of the screen:

  • Flight Number & Call sign (e.g., AFR1234)
  • Departure & Arrival Airports with scheduled departure times and estimated flight duration
  • Alternate Airport(s) with distance and reserve fuel requirements
  • Cruising Altitude / Initial Flight Level (e.g., FL350)
  • Airframe Type & Registration

docs.title: 2. Fuel & Weight Breakdown
docs.text:
Summarizes planned fuel figures and weights for easy cross-checking with your MCDU:

  • Block Fuel: Total fuel required on board before pushback.
  • Trip Fuel: Calculated burn for the planned route.
  • Contingency & Reserve Fuel: FAR/EASA regulatory reserves.
  • Alternate Fuel: Fuel required to divert to the planned alternate.
  • Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW): Planned aircraft empty weight plus payload.
  • Takeoff Weight (TOW): Calculated weight at brake release.

docs.title: 3. Route Navigation Log (Navlog)
docs.text:
Provides a scrollable navigation log listing:

  • Every airway, fix, and waypoint along the cleared routing.
  • Minimum Safe Altitudes (MSA) and planned flight levels.
  • Distance, heading, and estimated ground speed for each leg.
  • Forecast winds aloft (direction and speed) and temperature deviations (ISA DEV).

docs.title: 4. Weather, METAR & TAF
docs.text:
Aggregates real-time weather reports for all airports along your itinerary:

  • Departure Weather: Raw METAR, decoded wind, altimeter setting (QNH/inHg), temperature, and runway surface reports.
  • Destination Weather: Current conditions and terminal aerodrome forecasts (TAF).
  • Enroute Alternates: Quick-reference weather cards for emergency diversion planning.

docs.title: One-Click Sync to Weight & Balance
docs.text:
At the top of the SimBrief screen, click the Send to Weight & Balance button.

This automatically populates the passenger count, cargo weight, and block fuel values into the EFB Weight & Balance calculator without manual typing.

docs.title: Takeoff Performance Calculator
docs.text: The Takeoff Performance application computes accurate departure numbers tailored to your active Airbus airframe, gross weight, weather conditions, and runway dimensions.

docs.title: Operating Overview
docs.text:
To perform a takeoff calculation:

  1. Enter your departure airport and select the active runway.
  2. Verify atmospheric conditions (wind, temperature, barometric pressure).
  3. Confirm aircraft configuration (takeoff weight, packs, anti-ice).
  4. Tap Calculate.
  5. Review the resulting FLEX temperature, V-speeds, and trim settings.
  6. Transfer values directly into the aircraft FMGS.

docs.title: 1. Airport & Runway Selection
docs.text:
• Airport ICAO: Enter your 4-letter departure airport code (e.g., LFPG, KJFK, EGLL).
  • Runway: Select your departure runway from the dropdown menu. The calculator automatically retrieves:
  • Takeoff Run Available (TORA) and Takeoff Distance Available (TODA).
  • Runway elevation and slope.
  • Heading and magnetic variation.
  • Surface Condition: Select DRY, WET, or contaminated (water, slush, snow).

docs.title: 2. Environmental & Weather Data
docs.text:
• Wind Direction & Speed: In degrees magnetic and knots (e.g., 260/12).
  • Outside Air Temperature (OAT): In degrees Celsius.
  • QNH / Altimeter: In hPa or inHg.
  • Auto-Fill from Simulator: Click Sync Weather to automatically read current X-Plane 12 atmospheric datarefs at your airport.

docs.title: 3. Aircraft Configuration
docs.text:
• Takeoff Weight (TOW): Read automatically from the aircraft or entered manually.
  • Flap Configuration: Select AUTO (optimizer chooses best setting), CONF 1+F, CONF 2, or CONF 3.
  • Air Conditioning (Packs): Toggle between ON (standard operations) and OFF (high-performance departures).
  • Anti-Ice: Toggle OFF, ENG ONLY, or ENG + WING.

docs.title: Calculation Results
docs.text:
After tapping Calculate, the application displays:

  • Thrust Rating:
  • FLEX Temp: The calculated assumed temperature (e.g., FLEX 58°C) for reduced engine wear and fuel conservation.
  • TOGA: Indicated automatically if the runway length, high altitude, or high ambient temperature requires full takeoff thrust.
  • V-Speeds:
  • V1 (Decision Speed): Maximum speed to initiate an abort or continue the takeoff.
  • VR (Rotation Speed): Speed to initiate pitch rotation.
  • V2 (Takeoff Safety Speed): Climb speed with one engine inoperative.
  • Flaps & Horizontal Stabilizer Trim (THS):
  • Optimum flap configuration (e.g., CONF 1+F).
  • Trimmable Horizontal Stabilizer setting (e.g., UP 0.8 or DN 0.4), calculated directly from your takeoff center of gravity (CG).
  • Runway Margins:
  • Required takeoff runway distance versus available distance, with safety margins displayed in meters and feet.

docs.title: One-Click MCDU Scratchpad Sync
docs.text:
AlphaFloor EFB allows direct synchronization of performance data into the ToLiss FMGS:

  1. On the calculator results card, tap Send to MCDU.
  2. In the aircraft cockpit, navigate the MCDU to the PERF -> TAKE OFF page.
  3. Tap the line select keys (LSK 1L for V1, LSK 2L for VR, LSK 3L for V2, LSK 4R for FLEX TEMP, and LSK 3R for FLAPS/THS).
  4. The values transfer seamlessly from the EFB into the flight computer without manual keypad entry.

docs.title: Weight & Balance
docs.text: The Weight & Balance application provides interactive cabin boarding, cargo distribution, fuel planning, and real-time center of gravity (CG) envelope visualization.

docs.title: Operating Overview
docs.text:
To configure the aircraft payload and balance:

  1. Adjust passenger boarding numbers across cabin zones.
  2. Distribute freight across forward and aft cargo compartments.
  3. Set your required fuel quantity.
  4. Verify that the Center of Gravity (% MAC) remains within certified operational limits.
  5. Tap Apply to Aircraft to synchronize values directly into the simulator.

docs.title: 1. Passenger Seating
docs.text:
Passengers can be distributed across cabin sections (Forward, Mid, and Aft):

  • Each passenger is calculated at the standard European airline average of 100 kg (75 kg passenger weight plus 25 kg checked baggage).
  • Use the plus/minus stepper buttons or drag the cabin sliders to set your passenger load.
  • A quick-fill Board 100%, Board 75%, or Board Random button is available for rapid flight preparation.

docs.title: 2. Cargo Compartments
docs.text:
• Forward Cargo Hold (FWD): Cargo loaded forward of the wings, bringing the Center of Gravity forward.
  • Aft Cargo Hold (AFT): Cargo loaded behind the wings, moving the Center of Gravity aft.
  • Bulk Hold: Dedicated compartment for late bags and crew luggage.
  • The system enforces individual hold structural weight limits for each aircraft type.

docs.title: Fuel Planning
docs.text:
• Total Fuel Slider: Set total fuel in kilograms or pounds.
  • Automatic Tank Distribution: The application distributes fuel across outer wing tanks, inner wing tanks, center tanks, and trim tanks (on A330/A340) in strict accordance with standard Airbus fuel feeding logic.

docs.title: Dynamic Center of Gravity Envelope
docs.text:
A live graphical chart displays your aircraft position within the certified flight envelope:

  • Vertical Axis: Total Aircraft Gross Weight (kg).
  • Horizontal Axis: Center of Gravity expressed as a percentage of Mean Aerodynamic Chord (% MAC).
  • ZFWCG Point: The yellow marker shows your Zero Fuel Weight Center of Gravity.
  • TOCG Point: The green marker shows your Takeoff Center of Gravity.
  • Burn Vector Line: A line traces the migration of your Center of Gravity as fuel is consumed during flight, ensuring the aircraft never exceeds aft or forward limits before landing.

docs.title: Synchronization with Aircraft
docs.text:
• Send to Aircraft: Tapping this button instantly updates the ToLiss internal weight, payload, and fuel datarefs. There is no need to open the external aircraft configuration menu.
  • Read from Aircraft: Pulls the current simulator payload and fuel state into the EFB display.
